name: Javan
overview: Javan is identified in Scripture as a son of Japheth and an ancestor of the Greek peoples, with his descendants including Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim, indicating a lineage connected to maritime nations (Genesis 10:2, 4). He is also associated with trade and commerce, as Ezekiel describes Javan among the merchants engaged in trading goods such as brass, iron, cassia, and calamus, highlighting his role in ancient economic networks (Ezekiel 27:13, 19). Additionally, Isaiah portrays Javan as a distant nation among the Gentiles to whom God's glory will be declared, emphasizing the spread of His fame beyond Israel (Isaiah 66:19). Daniel's reference to the king of Grecia as a rough goat further connects Javan to the Greek world, underscoring his significance in biblical history and prophecy (Daniel 8:21).
